answer: Charge every new identity a real compute cost: before an agent can join, it must solve a proof-of-work puzzle tied to a public beacon, a fresh random seed published each epoch. The puzzle is cheap for one honest agent, like cracking a single walnut, but an attacker trying to grow a vine of ten thousand fake identities must pay that cost ten thousand times over. No stake or reputation can be reused across the fakes, so mass forgery becomes economically ruinous while genuine newcomers barely notice the fee.
